speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe when the rash first appeared and whether it is painful or just itchy? Also, have you started any new medications or supplements in the last two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any red spots on the palms of your hands or soles of your feet, and are there any blisters or pustules on the rash? Also, has anyone else in her household or school been sick with similar symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and are the spots on her trunk and limbs lacy or net-like in pattern? Also, has she had any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, preceded by mild prodromal symptoms, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
